rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A khalīfa succeeds another person in the work that person had been doing; this explains humanity as generations succeeding one another.
rows.anchor: جمع خليفة , وهو الذي يقوم بعد الإنسان بما كان قائما به

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: He explains that khulafāʾ is the plural of khalīf.
rows.anchor: الخلفاء جمع خليف - قال الأصبهاني

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Each age succeeds the previous one; some generations honor their predecessors, while others are base and disgraceful, and the virtuous and vile each test their age.
rows.anchor: أهل كل عصر خليفة عمن تقدمهم , فمن قوم هم لسلفهم جمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's repeated deaths and succession keep even many generations from filling the earth; without death, reproduction over time would outgrow it, though humans began as a small part of its soil.
rows.anchor: لإماتة كل قرن واستخلاف من بعدهم عنهم , ولو لم يمتهم لم تسعهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone lets people inhabit and manage their portion of the earth, so they owe Him gratitude rather than disbelief.
rows.anchor: فيما أنتم فيه منها لا غيره تتصرفون فيه بما قدرتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief harms only the disbeliever, who repudiates a precious blessing despite knowing that God alone enabled it.
rows.anchor: بعد علمه بأن الله هو الذي مكنه لا غيره , واحتقر هذه النعمة السنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here kāfirūn means those who cover the truth; their disbelief is entrenched, unlike a temporary disbelief that might end in faith.
rows.anchor: لا يزيد من كفر قد يكون كفره غير راسخ فيسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disbelief increases only maqt: God deals with them as one who hates and despises intensely, the consequence signified by the divine attribute.
rows.anchor: أي لأنه يعاملهم معاملة من يبغض ويحتقر أشد بغض واحتقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine descriptions convey their ultimate consequences and are framed in their harshest sense to repel people from the causes of such consequences.
rows.anchor: المراد من هذه الصفات في حق الله تعالى غاياتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers use the term nikāḥ al-maqt for marrying their fathers' wives, yet show no concern about earning God's contempt despite His beneficence.
rows.anchor: وكانوا ينكحون نساء الآباء مع أنهم يسمونه نكاح المقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief brings loss in this world and the next, in wealth and self, the ultimate result of divine contempt.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا والآخرة في المال والنفس وهو نهاية ما يفعله الماقت بالممقوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners belong to the worshippers, since they share in worshippers' wealth and deeds; they have taken nothing from God's dominion.
rows.anchor: لم ينالوا شيئا من شركته لأنهم ما نقصوه شيئا من ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to show what the idols created exposes the claim of partnership as baseless: only a creator can rightly be worshipped as creator.
rows.anchor: أي لتصح لكم دعوى الشركة فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to show the idols emphasizes their lowliness, since anyone can see them and know they create nothing; God is unlike them.
rows.anchor: بحيث يراهم كل من يقصد رؤيتهم ويعلم أنه لا خلق لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast makes it absurd to equate the uncreative with God, who creates every creature and is known by all to do so.
rows.anchor: فكيف يكون من لا يخلق كمن يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired questions use ellipsis: the earth's partnership question is omitted because the heaven question states it, and the second command to show is omitted because the first supplies it.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : حذف أولا الاستفهام عن الشركة في الأرض لدلالة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge also asks whether God gave them a book proving partnership; no such revealed proof supports their claim.
rows.anchor: أي الشركاء أو المشركين بهم لما لنا من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular reading means a clear proof, while the other reading has the plural bayyināt, meaning multiple clear proofs in the book.
rows.anchor: أي حجة ظاهرة , وبينات - على القراءة الأخرى , أي دلائل واضحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sensible person should allege a partnership without knowing it, even if the identity of the other partner is unknown.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي لعاقل أن يدعي شركة لشيء حتى يعلم الشركة وإن جهل عين المشارك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is also called Yā-Sīn, the Heart, the Repelling, the Decisive, and the Comprehensive.
rows.anchor: وتسمى القلب والدافعة والقاضية والمعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its central purpose is to establish the Messenger's mission to Mecca and Quraysh, whom the author calls the heart of the Arabs and humanity; their reform or corruption affects those around them.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات الرسالة التي هي روح الوجود وقلب جميع الحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The message establishes divine oneness and warns of the Gathering, whose unseen reality reforms creation; attention to its causes brings eternal felicity, while neglect brings lasting misery.
rows.anchor: مع ستره عن العيان الذي هو من خواص القلب - صلاح الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart imagery fits the surah: the human heart is hidden from sight yet contains subtle and manifest faculties that can repair or ruin the body, as the unseen afterlife can determine human destiny.
rows.anchor: قلب الإنسان غائبا عن الإحساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā-Sīn will be explained as signaling the surah's heart-like character and its emphasis on resurrection; the other names describe protection, fulfillment of good, and comprehensive blessing.
rows.anchor: وأما يس فسيأتي بيانه من جهة إشارته إلى سر كونها قلبا المشير إلى البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah explicitly depicts the trumpet blast and bodily resurrection, making the afterlife its central concern.
rows.anchor: التصريح بالمعاد الجسماني والاستدلال عليه بالدليل

rows.speaker: أبو نصر الفارابي
rows.claim: Al-Fārābī wished Aristotle had seen the argument: God first created and animated bones, so He can create and animate them again after they decay.
rows.anchor: نقل أبا نصر الفارابي - الذي وسم بأنه المعلم الثاني - كان يقول

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that al-Tirmidhī transmitted the Prophet's saying that every thing has a heart and Yā-Sīn is the Qur'an's heart.
rows.anchor: فيما رواه الترمذي عن أنس رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: معقل بن يسار
rows.claim: A report from Maʿqil says Yā-Sīn is the Qur'an's heart; whoever recites it seeking God and the Hereafter is forgiven, and it should be read over the dying.
rows.anchor: عن معقل بن يسار رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: شهاب الدين البوصيري
rows.claim: Al-Būṣīrī says a report from Abū Hurayra collected by al-Bazzār supports the heart-of-the-Qur'an report.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا الحافظ شهاب الدين البوصيري : وله شاهد من حديث أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: العزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains that Yā-Sīn is the Qur'an's heart because sound faith depends on recognizing resurrection, which this surah establishes especially forcefully; al-Rāzī approves the explanation.
rows.anchor: قال العزالي فيه : إن ذلك - أي كونها قلبا - لأن الإيمان صحته بالاعتراف بالحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah establishes the three foundations—oneness, prophethood, and resurrection—with strong proofs, beginning with the Messenger and ending with God's dominion and return to Him.
rows.anchor: إن هذه السورة ليس فيها إلا تقرير الأصول الثلاثة : الوحدانية والرسالة والحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its focus on inward assent explains the name Heart, though the claim that it contains no duties of speech or action is challenged by its commands to worship, give, and follow the straight path.
rows.anchor: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report to recite Yā-Sīn over the dying is transmitted by Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, Ibn Ḥibbān, and al-Ḥākim from Maʿqil.
rows.anchor: والحديث الذي ذكره رواه أحمد وأبو داود والنسائي وابن ماجه وابن حبان والحاكم

rows.speaker: ابن القطان
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qaṭṭān judged the dying-person report weak, and al-Dāraquṭnī also weakens it.
rows.anchor: وضعفه الدارقطني ، وأسند صاحب الفردوس عن أبي الدرداء

rows.speaker: صاحب الفردوس
rows.claim: The author notes a report in al-Firdaws from Abū al-Dardāʾ and Abū Dharr alone.
rows.anchor: وأسند صاحب الفردوس عن أبي الدرداء وأبي ذر وحده

rows.speaker: صفوان بن عمرو
rows.claim: Aḥmad transmits that elders said reciting Yā-Sīn beside a dead person lightens the person's state; Ibn Ḥibbān interprets this as the person near death.
rows.anchor: كانت المشيخة يقولون : إذا قرئت يس عند الميت خفف عنه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's explicit resurrection teaching grounds Quranic reminders of the Hereafter: attending to them reforms both lives, while neglect corrupts them.
rows.anchor: واستمد من هذا التصريح بالحشر كل ما انبث في القرآن من ذكر الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā-Sīn gathers themes of the Fātiḥa: God's names and dominion, worship on the straight path, the blessed and the doomed, and the three foundations of faith.
rows.anchor: والأمر بالعبادة بسلوك الصراط المستقيم ، وتفضيل أهل النعيم وأهل الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is a source of life and reform for the spirit; resurrection is its goal, and its conclusion affirms the Prophet as the heart and finest part of creation.
rows.anchor: البعث غايته ، وأن الخاتم لها إنسان عين الموجودات وقلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its opening disconnected letters stir the mind and span both dotted and undotted, voiced and unvoiced letters.
rows.anchor: مع جمع ما افتتحت به السورة من الحروف المقطعة المنثورة أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the mouths of those who lied, while hands and feet speak truth about their deeds; the direct actors' speech is confession and the feet's speech is testimony.
rows.anchor: وكان الروغان والكذب والفساد إنما يكون باللسان المعرب عن القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: speech is assigned first to hands because they acted, and testimony to feet because they were present, with the reverse terms understood.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : أثبت الكلام للأيدي أولا لأنها كانت مباشرة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: In a sound Muslim report, a servant asks to testify only through himself; God seals his mouth and orders his limbs to speak of his deeds, then releases him to rebuke them.
rows.anchor: في صحيحه عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال : يقول العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mouth is sealed so the person cannot interrupt or make idle, contentious talk while the limbs testify.
rows.anchor: السر في الختم على فيه منعه من أن يلغط حال شهادتها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the judgment after resurrection, the surah threatens blinding and transformation before death, showing that God can remove physical sight as He veils inner sight.
rows.anchor: أتبعه آية الختم بالطمس والمسخ قبل الموت تهديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense wording of God's willing makes the threat sound possible at any moment and intensifies its force.
rows.anchor: ليتوقع في كل حين , فيكون أبلغ في التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to race toward their familiar path implies hurried flight, but the blinded people cannot see it and collide into danger.
rows.anchor: الطريق الواضح الذي ألفوه واعتادوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks how they could see after their eyes were erased, so they cannot find the path and instead stumble into destruction.
rows.anchor: أي فلم يهتدوا للصراط لعدم إبصارهم بل تصادموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God willed, He could turn them into inert matter in the very places they occupied before moving, leaving them unable to move forward.
rows.anchor: حولناهم إلى الجمادية فأبطلنا منهم الحركة الإدراية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿba's reading from ʿĀṣim has makānatihim in the singular, locating each person at his own fixed place.
rows.anchor: قراءة شعبة عن عاصم ( مكانتهم ) ودل على أن المراد التحويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would also never return to their prior condition; the imperfect verb conveys the lasting impossibility, which the verbal noun ruǧūʿan would not express.
rows.anchor: لم يفد هذا المعنى النفيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Long life reverses human development: people advance through infancy and maturity, then lose the faculties and knowledge they gained.
rows.anchor: نرده على عقبه نازلا في المدارج التي أصعدناه فيها فلا يعلم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled reading of nunakkisuhu by ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza points to differing degrees of decline among people.
rows.anchor: وقراءة عاصم وحمزة بضم أوله وفتح ثانيه وكسر الكاف مشددة دالة على تفاوت الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says decline occurs in the created form, avoiding the mistaken implication that God has a created form of His own.
rows.anchor: لئلا يظن أن المراد أن المعمر له خلق أنشأه وأبدعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Age-related reversal proves God's power to transform creation in reverse as well as to resurrect; its familiarity makes people take it lightly, while rarer transformations seem remote.
rows.anchor: ومن قدر على مثل هذا التحويل من حالة إلى أخرى لم تكن طردا وعكسا قدر على مثل ما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading addresses people indirectly, while the Madinan readers and Yaʿqūb use direct address, which is more tender and makes the admonition inclusive.
rows.anchor: ولفتا إلى الخطاب عند المدنيين ويعقوب لأنه أقرب إلى الاستعطاف

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some spiritual knowers say “in creation” restricts decline to the body: bodily weakening is inevitable, but knowledge and obedience may grow with age.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العارفين : قيد بالخلق احترازا عن الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary human faculties level off around forty-two; bodily senses stop growing and moral qualities develop only through experience and effort.
rows.anchor: من استوفى سن الصبا والشباب اثنين وأربعين سنة حسمت غرائزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets receive exceptional knowledge, wisdom, and strength that do not decline with age, unlike ordinary people; reports of the Prophet's walk, wrestling, and household strength illustrate this.
rows.anchor: الأنبياء عليهم السلام تظهر عليهم غرائز العلوم والحكم وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In an authentic report from Abū Hurayra, Moses struck the Angel of Death and injured his eye; after being offered years for each hair covered by his hand on an ox, Moses chose death.
rows.anchor: ورد في الصحيح من حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن ملك الموت عليه السلام أرسل إلى موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses died at 120 without decline in his faculties; the prophets' exemption from ordinary aging honors them and signals their truthfulness.
rows.anchor: وكان موسى يوم قضي ابن مائة وعشرين سنة , لم يضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context implies that God aged the Prophet without reversing his faculties, granting him unparalleled virtues and a Qur'an beyond human and jinn capacity.
rows.anchor: عمرناه وما نكسناه بل منحناه غرائز من الفضائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's lack of poetry is evidence against his opponents: he passed childhood and youth without composing a verse, though poetic talent cannot ordinarily arise after the age when faculties plateau.
rows.anchor: بيت شعر ما يرى لكم ولأمثالكم فيه من المفاخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry requires artificial adherence to meter and rhyme that can distort meaning; God did not teach the Prophet this inferior craft but gave him eloquence and graceful, forceful expression in any form.
rows.anchor: لا يليق بجنابنا لأنه لا يفرح به إلا من يريد ترويج كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's wisdom and concise, noble speech came through inspiration and Gabriel's instruction; he chose the easier of two options unless it involved sin or severing kinship.
rows.anchor: ثم بما ألقاه إليه جبريل عليه السلام مما أمرنا له به من جوامع الكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited line in al-Ḥamāsa is attributed to an unnamed man of Banū Qurayʿ; the poem contrasts wealth with poverty and honor with disgrace.
rows.anchor: عزاه في الحماسة في أوائل باب الأدب إلى رجل من بني قريع لم يسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and poverty are not innate traits: a vigorous poor youth may become rich in old age, while a wealthy person may have blameworthy character and a poor person admirable morals.
rows.anchor: كثيرا ما رأينا من فاته الغنى شابا جلدا وناله شيخا ضعيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muruwwa means humanity and praiseworthy conduct; one who possesses it by nature practices it young, while a person lacking it cannot acquire it merely by growing older.
rows.anchor: المروءة هي الإنسانية , وهي كل أمر هنيء حميد المغبة جميل العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah shows God keeps His promises, overcomes everything, need not hurry, and places matters in their proper settings, as discerning people recognize.
rows.anchor: أنه غالب لكل شيء ، فلا يعجل لأنه لا يفوته شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Zumar evokes groups led to their prepared afterlife homes after warning, judged by their deeds, with justice for the people of Hell and grace for the righteous.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه أنزل كلا من المحشورين داره المعدة له بعد الإعذار في الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative names Tanzīl and al-Ghuraf likewise point to God's judgment of the two groups in fiery canopies and luminous chambers; the latter name uses the nobler component.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حكمه سبحانه في الفريقين أهل الظلل النارية والغرف النورية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening blessing describes God's complete word, wisely placed universal mercy, and special guidance that gives His chosen servants obedience.
rows.anchor: رحمته العامة أحكم وضع فدق لذي الأفهام سره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God needs nothing and their own experience shows His rule over everything, the claim that He has a child or partner is false and He declares Himself free of such نقص.
rows.anchor: لقيام الأدلة على عدم الحاجة إلى شيء أصلا فضلا عن الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is indivisible and without likeness, spouse, or child; His absolute oneness and dominion mean He has no need of anything.
rows.anchor: لا ينقسم أصلا , ولا يكون له مثل فلا يكون له صاحبة ولا ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His overpowering dominion subjects everything, including the alleged gods, continuously and repeatedly.
rows.anchor: فكل شيء تحت قهره آلهتهم وغيرها على سبيل التكرار والاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth were brought from nonexistence in truth, perfectly and without flaw, variation, or disorder.
rows.anchor: { بالحق } أي خلقا متلبسا بالأمر الثابت الذي ليس بخيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated covering of night and day demonstrates divine power and subjugation even more strongly than the image of one entering the other.
rows.anchor: وكان التكوير - وهو إرادة الشيء على الشيء بسرعة وإحاطته به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takwīr depicts night rapidly wrapping over and covering day, then day covering night; each replaces and conceals the other in a repeated cycle.
rows.anchor: يلف ويلوي ويدير فيغطي مع السرعة والعلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation also includes each light period lengthening as it takes time from the other, like clothing wrapped over what it covers.
rows.anchor: ويدخل في هذا الزيادة في كل منهما بما ينقص من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering of night before day follows the order of creation, since darkness precedes the light of sunrise.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قدم آية النهار فقال معبرا بالماضي بخلقه الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subdued the sun and moon, compelling each to follow its known course and fixed limit without benefit to the objects themselves.
rows.anchor: ذلل وأكره وقهر وكلف لما يريد من غير نفع للمسخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both bodies run by God's irrevocable decree, and their courses illustrate alternating human states of contraction and expansion, cognition and ignorance.
rows.anchor: بقضائنا الذي لا مرد له , وهذا آية لاختلاف أحوال العبد

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī maps the sky's cycles onto spiritual states: reason, knowledge, and recognition wax like stars, moons, and suns, while unity and connection alternate with doubt and separation.
rows.anchor: قاله القشيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is the endpoint of each orbit and motion; specifying the governing decree emphasizes God's domination more than naming an endpoint alone.
rows.anchor: لمنتهى الدور ومنقطع الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is mighty; His repeated forgiveness explains why He delays seizing sinners, while He may erase their sins inwardly and outwardly or punish them by His might.
rows.anchor: الذي له صفة الستر على الذنوب متكررة فيمحو ذنوب من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of animals and especially humans, with speech and inescapable bodily conditions, is a further sign of divine oneness and power; humanity comes from Adam, a single soul.
rows.anchor: { من نفس واحدة } هي آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to declare that he worships God alone with undiluted devotion, neither turning to another object nor worshipping for paradise or from fear of Hell.
rows.anchor: تخصيصا له بذلك , لا أنحو أصلا بالعبادة نحو غيره أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's fear is instead the fear of failing to give servitude its due before God's lordship and of losing divine beneficence.
rows.anchor: فإنما خوفي إعطاء المقام حقه من ذل العبودية وعز الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation to worship whatever they wish is a threat: worshipping anything beneath God risks losing His favor, and no beneficence exists apart from His.
rows.anchor: فإن عبادة ما دونه تؤدي إلى قطع إحسانه , ولا إحسان إلا إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers destroy themselves and their families at the Resurrection; if relatives are damned their loss is shared, and if they are saved there will be no reunion.
rows.anchor: أي لأنهم إن كانوا مثلهم فحالهم في الخسارة كحالهم , ولا يمكن أحدا منهم أن يواسي صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Resurrection is the decisive day, when what was lost cannot be repaired.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك اليوم هو الفيصل لا يمكن لما فات فيه تدارك أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative phrase identifies this as the uniquely manifest loss; the emphatic form khusrān intensifies its magnitude and reproach.
rows.anchor: أتى بصيغة الفعلان المفهم مطلقا للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire's canopies are both above and below the condemned, so they cannot find rest or a stable place amid the flames' violent rising and falling.
rows.anchor: يصعدهم اللهيب تارة , ويهبطهم انعكاسه عليهم برجوعه إليهم أخرى

rows.speaker: سمر بن جندب
rows.claim: In a long Bukhārī dream report, the Prophet sees naked men and women in a furnace-like hole whose flames raise them toward its narrow top and drop them back; they are identified as adulterers.
rows.anchor: في صحيحه عن سمر بن جندب رضي الله عنه قال : كان النبي صلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is meant to frighten servants who will heed it, strengthening their faith and leading them to seek refuge from the threatened punishment.
rows.anchor: الذين لهم أقلية الإقبال عليه ليزدادوا إيمانا فيعيذهم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to aid the messengers stands despite their enemies' threats, just as God gave guidance and scripture to Moses and granted him the eventual victory over Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: ولقد آتيناك الهدى والكتاب كما آتينا موسى , ولننصرنك مثل ما نصرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should endure their abuse because God brings events about in their proper settings through the causes established for this world.
rows.anchor: أي على أذاهم فإنا نوقع الأشياء في أتم محالها

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says patience while awaiting God's promise rises in proportion to a person's faith and certainty.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : الصبر في انتظار الموعود من الحق على حسب الإيمان والتصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness for the Prophet's “sin” means seeking forgiveness for every complete deed; he is already forgiven, and the wording teaches his community by example.
rows.anchor: وهو كل عمل كامل لأن ذلك غفر لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a complete deed a sin follows the maxim that the good deeds of the righteous are faults for those brought near to God.
rows.anchor: من باب ( حسنات الأبرار سيئات المقربين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to glorify God affirms His perfection and negates every defect; ascent in knowledge makes the creature's limits clearer.
rows.anchor: نزه ربك عن شائبة نقص كلما علمت بالصعود في مدارج الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evening and morning cycles show the Creator's ability to restore what has perished, supporting the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإن تقلبهما دائما دل على كمال مقلبهما وقدرته على إيجاد المعدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges the dawn and afternoon prayers, which angels of night and day witness; Ibn ʿAbbās instead says it refers to all five prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بل على الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no escape from error or the punishment it causes; therefore people must answer their Lord's call through the Messenger's commands.
rows.anchor: اطلبوا الإجابة وأوجدوها , ولفت القول إلى الوصف الإحساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must respond before the irreversible Day arrives; even a small act of good before death makes timely obedience urgent.
rows.anchor: يكون فيه ما لا يمكن معه فلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can reverse that Day because it comes from God, who possesses all majesty and whose decision none can overturn.
rows.anchor: وإذا لم يكن له مرد منه لم يكن مرد من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day there will be no refuge or fortress and no one can deny people's acts to rescue them: recorders and their own limbs will testify.
rows.anchor: لأن الحفظة يشهدون عليكم فإن صدقتموهم وإلا شهدت عليكم أعضاؤكم وجلودكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people turn away from the clear religion, the Messenger is not their guardian who can force obedience; his duty is only to convey, while guidance and misguidance belong to God.
rows.anchor: لما أرسلناك به , وأما الهداية والإضلال فإلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage continues by explaining that human beings, in their ignorance, can be lured by slight kindness into defying the Lord before whom mountains would tremble.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان لغلبه جهله وقلة عقله يجترئ بأدنى تأنيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers claim worldly life is the only life, though “worldly” is a relative description that itself suggests another, later life.
rows.anchor: مدلول هذا الوصف الذي هو أمر نسي لا يعقل إلا بالإضافة إلى حياة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their saying “we die and live” means some people die and others are born; they deny that the same person lives after death and reduce themselves to animal-like attention to particulars.
rows.anchor: تنزع الروح من بعض فيموت , وتنفخ في بعض آخر فيحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They attribute their eventual destruction to time, which overcomes people through successive changes and unpleasant events; the author connects dahr to the verb meaning to overcome.
rows.anchor: الزمان الطويل بغلبته علينا بتجدد إقباله وتجدد إدبارنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no knowledge, only conjecture based on observing human decline with age and the fact that no dead person has returned.
rows.anchor: بقرينة أن الإنسان كلما تقدم في السن ضعف , وأنه لم يرجع أحد من الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite clear proofs of resurrection, their only purported argument is the demand to bring their ancestors back, a response the author calls no real proof.
rows.anchor: ما كان حجتهم إلا أن قالوا ائتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers will be shown Hell like troops presented before a ruler, hearing its roar and seeing its flames and terror.
rows.anchor: عرض الجند على الملك فيسمعوا من تغيظها وزفيرها ويروا من لهيبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked whether the promised punishment is real, they admit and swear that it is; this confession comes too late to benefit them.
rows.anchor: أي مصدقين حيث لا ينفع التصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to taste punishment because of their persistent disbelief in the world of action.
rows.anchor: باشروه مباشرة الذائق باللسان ثم صرح بالسبب

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī defines patience as standing firm under God's decree without complaint or resistance.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : والصبر هو الوقوف بحكم الله والثبات من غير بث ولا استكراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's command to be patient resumes the call to endure the hardships of conveying the message.
rows.anchor: أي على مشاق ما ترى في تبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent reading makes min partitive: “the resolute messengers” are foremost law-bearing messengers who established their laws, commonly Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم أصحاب الشرائع الذين اجتهدوا في تأسيس قواعدها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase means all messengers; Ibn al-Anbārī adopts this view and takes min as generic rather than partitive.
rows.anchor: وقال : ( من ) للتجنيس لا للتبعيض

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits the view that all prophets are meant except Jonah.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الجوزي : حكاه الثعلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The identities of the resolute messengers are disputed, but the partitive interpretation is the most famous and, in the author's judgment, clearest.
rows.anchor: والخلاف في تعيينهم كثير منتشر هذا القول أشهر ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not hasten the opponents' punishment or act against them before the proper time; this restrains haste, a grave vice, and completes the virtue of patience.
rows.anchor: نهاه عن العجلة التي هي من أمهات الرذائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised event may be seen at death or in the afterlife; it warns sinners and gives good news to the obedient, who will feel worldly life lasted only a brief hour.
rows.anchor: الدين في الدنيا والبعث في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “an hour of daylight” both verifies the short duration and belittles it, since sāʿa can otherwise mean a long period.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الساعة قد يراد بها الجنس وقد تطلق على الزمن الطويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a clear, sufficient warning that guides people to the Mighty and Wise's lasting reward; those it does not guide are people whom God has ordained for misery.
rows.anchor: من الظهور وانتشار النور بحيث يرد المنذرين ويوصلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the deeply rebellious are destroyed; the passive form focuses on the outcome and signals that their destruction is easy for God.
rows.anchor: بني للمفعول من أهلك , لأن المحذور الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's close connects back to its opening warning and proofs, and links its themes of resurrection, creation, revelation, divine power, and wisdom into a coherent ending.
rows.anchor: فقد التحم هذا الآخر بذاك الأول التي تليها أحسن التئام

none: bare heading for the next surah
